results.content: # Metadata: Controlled Vocabularies. Library resource for learning about metadata and its practical application. ## Controlled Vocabularies. In addition to selecting a metadata standard or schema, whenever possible you should use a controlled vocabulary. **A controlled vocabulary provides a consistent way to describe data**. Examples of controlled vocabularies include subject headings, thesauri, ontologies, and taxonomies. Using a controlled vocabulary will aid in searching and finding your data and will make your data more shareable with researchers in the same discipline. ## Controlled Vocabulary Resources. * Library of Congress Authorities for subject heading. * United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) thesauri. * Rare Books and Special Collections Vocabulary. * International Classification of Disease (ICD). * Logical Observation Identifiers Names, and Codes (LOINC) - for tests, observations and measurements. * SNOMED-CT (for clinical terms). * The Getty Institute Thesaurus of Geographical Names. ## Resources for Inclusive Description. Examples of Inclusive Knowledge Organization:. * X̱wi7x̱wa Library Indigenous Knowledge Organization. * National Library of New Zealand Ngā Upoko Tukutuku. * Human Rights Campaign Glossary of Terms. * Villanova University School of Business Glossary of Terms. * Last Updated: Mar 20, 2025 3:01 PM.

results.title: What Is a Controlled Vocabulary? — Backlog • Archivists & Historians
results.content: # What Is a Controlled Vocabulary? A controlled vocabulary is a foundational tool in metadata creation and information organization. ### Controlled Vocabularies and Taxonomies. Together, controlled vocabularies and schemas help standardize description, improve discoverability, and connect collections across institutions. ### Where We See Controlled Vocabularies. ### How Controlled Vocabularies Work with Metadata Schemas. To understand how controlled vocabularies interact with metadata schemas, picture a metadata schema as a series of compartments or fields. Even if your metadata schema changes and includes more fields, such as stamen or leaf vein color, the same controlled vocabulary can still apply. Controlled vocabularies help solve common metadata problems. ### Examples of Controlled Vocabularies. Examples of well-known controlled vocabularies include LCSH and LCNAF (Library of Congress Name Authority File), the AAT, ULAN, the Thesaurus of Geographic Names (TGN), and the Medical Subject Headings (MeSH). Watch our recorded webinar on controlled vocabularies, where we cover examples, tools, and tips for implementing these systems in archives, libraries, and museums.

results.content: ## Sample and Data Relationship Format (SDRF-Proteomics). The Sample and Data Relationship Format (SDRF-Proteomics) is a tab-delimited text format that describes the relationship between samples and data files. The SDRF-Proteomics is the format that aims to store the relation between the samples analyzed in the experiment and the corresponding instrument files. **Figure 1**: SDRF-Proteomics file format stores the information of the sample and its relation to the data files in the dataset. The file format includes not only information about the sample but also about how the data was acquired and processed. ### SDRF-Proteomics Specification. The SDRF-Proteomics format describes the sample characteristics and the relationships between samples and data files included in a dataset. The information in SDRF files is organised so that it follows the natural flow of a proteomics experiment. The main requirements to be fulfilled for SDRF-Proteomics format are:. The SDRF file is a tab-delimited format where each ROW corresponds to a relationship between a Sample and a Data file (and MS signal corresponding to labelling in the context of multiplexed experiments). SDRF-Proteomics is fully compatible with the SDRF file format part of MAGE-TAB. MAGE-TAB is the file format used to store metadata and sample information for transcriptomics experiments. When the proteomeXchange project file is converted to idf file (project description in MAGE-TAB) and is combined with the SDRF-Proteomics a valid MAGE-TAB is obtained. SDRF-Proteomics sample information can be embedded into mzTab metadata files. The sample metadata in mzTab contains properties as the columns in the SDRF-Proteomics and values as Sample cell values. The SDRF-Proteomics aims to capture the sample metadata and its relationship with the data files (e.g. raw files from mass spectrometers). ### Ontologies/Controlled Vocabularies Supported. The list of ontologies/controlled vocabularies (CV) supported are:. The official website for SDRF-Proteomics project is . The website includes the specification of the file format, examples and tools to validate the files. Multiple tools have been implemented to validate SDRF-Proteomics files for users familiar with Python and Java:. * sdrf-pipelines (Python—): This tool allows validating an SDRF-Proteomics file. * jsdrf (Java—): This Java library and tool allows validating SDRF-Proteomics files.

results.content: * Technical, Rights and Preservation Metadata. ## Introduction. ****Controlled vocabulary** is a standardized set of terms used to organize knowledge for subsequent retrieval. It can facilitate search and browsing. It can be universally agreed on or locally created.**. **What to consider in applying or designing a thesauri for your project:**. * Scope of the material (core and surrounding topics, your purpose, existing thesauri and your resource);. * Your project needs and intended audience;. * Funder requirements and institutional expectation;. * What types of controlled vocabularies you may need: subject, genre, physical format, personal names, organization names, events…. * When choosing particular terms over others, consider three warrants: literary warrant (discipline and field literature), user warrant and organizational warrant. (Gazan, CONTROLLED VOCABULARY & THESAURUS DESIGN). ## Controlled Vocabularies and Thesauri. * AGROVOC (Agricultural Organization of the United Nations Vocabulary). * CAB Thesaurus (for life sciences, technology and social sciences). * Getty Institute Art and Architecture Thesaurus Online. * Getty Institute Thesaurus of Geographic Names. * ICD (International Classification of Diseases). * IEEE Thesaurus (Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers). * Library of Congress Authorities for Subject Headings. * Library of Congress Thesaurus for Graphic Materials. * Logical Observation Identifiers Names, and Codes (LOINC). * Rare Books and Manuscripts Section (RBMS) Controlled Vocabularies. * SNOMED CT (Systematized Nomenclature of Medicine - Clinical Terms). * USDA National Agricultural Library Agriculture Thesaurus. **Name Authority Files and Name Linked Data Sets:**. * Virtual International Authority File (VIAF). * ORCID (Open Researcher and Contributor ID). * MARC Code List for Countries. * MARC Code List for Languages. * MARC Source Codes for Vocabularies, Rules, and Schemes. **For digital and online resources:**. * Library of Congress Linked Data Service. * Resource Description and Access Toolkit. * searchFAST (Search Faceted Application of Subject Terminology). * The Open Biological and Biomedical Ontologies. * Last Updated: Aug 20, 2024 1:45 PM.
